column3: “It was reversed” is rendered “it was turned to the contrary,” and “domineer” as “gain the mastery.”
“Not anyone stood” is rendered “no one could stand.”
“The doers of the work” is rendered “those who were doing the king's business,” and “supporting” as “assisted.”
“His report was going” is rendered “his fame spread,” and “was going and becoming great” as “became greater and greater.”
“A striking down of sword and slaughter and destruction” is rendered “with the sword, killing and destroying.”
“The citadel” is rendered “the capital.”

“The rural villagers who were dwelling in the cities of the open regions” is rendered “the Jews of the rural areas, who live in the rural towns.” “Portions” is rendered “portions of food.”
“The words” is rendered “these events.”
“Impose on them” is rendered “obliging them,” and “in every year and year” as “annually.”
“Had rest from” is rendered “rid themselves of,” and “a day good” as “a holiday.” “The needy” is rendered “the poor.”
“Accepted” is rendered “undertook.”
“Opposer” is rendered “adversary,” and “trouble” as “disturb.”
“When it came before the king” is rendered “when it came to the king's attention”; the Hebrew may mean “when she came,” and the meaning is uncertain.
“The words of the letter” is rendered “the instructions in this letter.”
“Imposed and accepted” is rendered “established and made a custom.” “According to their writing” is rendered “according to their regulation.”
“Clan and clan” is rendered “every family.”
“All authority” is rendered “full authority.” The word “second” is difficult here, and the meaning is uncertain.
